title: Lane shaping: end-to-end tenant throttles, soft quota borrowing, and safety-net preemption
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: multi-tenant Dedicated GPU pools occasionally see noisy-tenant events where a single tenant's bursty workload drives queueing and kernel contention, causing other tenants to miss throughput SLAs and increasing per-token cost. Existing soft-quota enforcement is reactive and lacks clear borrowing/fallback semantics.

Goal: implement an end-to-end lane shaping system that enforces per-tenant throughput budgets, enables controlled soft borrowing, and surfaces a safety-net preemption lane for SLA-sensitive tenants. The design must integrate with the autoscaler so lanes can expand/contract predictably, and ownership/telemetry must be visible in the Console.

Scope: runtime admission control (token-bucket lane shaper), quota manager (soft quota + borrow window + decay), safety-net preemption policy (whitelistable for enterprise customers), autoscaler hooks (scale-up signals when lanes hit sustained saturation), metrics and dashboards, and rollout plan (internal alpha -> canary customers -> full rollout).

Non-goals: per-request model-level throttling (out of scope for this ticket), persistent per-tenant node pinning, and changes to billing model.

Why unique: instead of static partitions, lane shaping provides dynamic, bandwidth-like isolation that adapts to workload patterns while still allowing short-term bursts under controlled borrowing. This balances utilization and predictability for customers on Dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime enforces per-tenant steady-state token rates and bucket burst capacity configurable per-plan (enterprise/standard).
Soft-borrowing allows up to 25% temporary capacity increase for standard tenants when pool utilization < 60%, decaying over 2 minutes. Configurable per-pool and per-tenant.
Safety-net preemption can preempt best-effort requests from non-whitelist tenants within 150ms of a high-priority tenant margin violation, with audit logs emitted.
Autoscaler receives lane saturation signals and can trigger controlled scale-up without violating node placement constraints in Dedicated pools.
Console shows per-tenant lane usage, borrowed tokens, preemption events, and suggested config changes in the Optimize tab.
End-to-end tests and integration benchmarks demonstrate recovery from a noisy neighbor event with >= 99% throughput SLA compliance for enterprise tenants under mixed workloads.
